methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $22M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 4 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Robotics & Manufacturing. Range: $1.1B - $2.0B.

data.narrative:
RISE Robotics is a Series A robotics and manufacturing company founded by Arron Acosta and Blake Sessions that has raised $22M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comparable universe of 9 private peers and 1 public company in the Robotics & Manufacturing sector, including Series B-stage companies such as Generalist AI, Bedrock Robotics, and Dexterity, as well as earlier-stage players like Walden Robotics.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-Progression modeling uses the $22M raised as a valuation proxy and applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical for Series A to next-stage progression, implying a value of $44M. Peer-Median analysis examines four same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables with a median valuation of $1.7B and a range spanning $1.1B to $2.0B. The peer set reflects heterogeneity in stage and valuation outcomes, with Walden Robotics at the lower end and Generalist AI at $2.0B.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $37M (low) to $2.0B (high), with a median of $872M. The wide spread reflects material uncertainty regarding RISE's market position and exit comparability relative to the peer set. Stage-Progression yields a conservative floor given early-stage positioning; Peer-Median carries execution risk, as comparable valuations may not reflect RISE's specific traction, technology, or capital efficiency. Further due diligence on revenue, unit economics, and market opportunity definition is required to narrow this range.
